title: Gaming Addiction Rises Among Japan's Youth
paragraphs: A growing number of young people in Japan may be addicted to video games, according to a new national survey.

The survey was carried out by the Kurihama Medical and Addiction Center, a hospital in Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, which specializes in treating addiction. It was conducted as a national research project. In January and February 2025, questionnaires were sent to about 9,000 people aged between 10 and 79 across the country, and 4,650 people gave valid answers. The results were announced in August 2026.

According to the survey, 10.3% of people aged between 10 and 29 were suspected of having gaming disorder, which is commonly known as gaming addiction. This was about double the result of a similar survey carried out in the 2018 fiscal year, which found that 5.1% of young people were suspected of having the condition.

Gaming disorder is a condition in which people put games ahead of other parts of their daily lives and continue playing even when it causes problems with their schoolwork or health. In 2019, the World Health Organization officially recognized it as a new type of addictive disorder.

The center believes that one reason for the increase is that it has become normal for children to use the internet and play games from a very young age. Because of this, more young people may be developing a tendency to become dependent on games.

However, Japan has only a small number of medical institutions that specialize in treating this kind of addiction, and experts say that support needs to be strengthened. The center has called on schools, families and local communities to work together to help prevent the problem.

Other research has also raised concerns. A separate survey published in 2026 found that 10.5% of people in their twenties in Japan had spent so much money on in-game purchases that they had trouble paying for their living costs.
